correctness.rationale: The critical scalar estimate is an exact operator-norm statement. For the K4 difference operator D, D*D=4I-J gives ||D||_2=2, while the row structure gives ||D||_infinity=2; Riesz--Thorin yields ||D||_p<=2 for every 2<=p<=infinity, and (1,1,-1,-1) gives equality. Applying this coordinatewise to four unit vectors gives sum_{i<j}||x_i-x_j||_p^p<=4*2^p. Power mean on the six distances gives the stated squared-distance upper bound. The centered three-coordinate sign tetrahedron has six equal distances 2(2/3)^(1/p), so every inequality is sharp. The p=infinity endpoint follows directly from diameter two.
risks: Riesz--Thorin is used as a standard finite-dimensional interpolation theorem; no stronger interpolation equality statement is assumed.
The finite checker samples intermediate exponents but the proof of all exponents is analytic, not numerical.

originality.rationale: The defining 2021 source was inspected at its abstract, Section 3 definition, universal estimates, Hilbert characterization, subsequent comparison results, and conclusion. It does not state the dimension-at-least-three all-p formula. Public-index searches covered the exact invariant name, ell_p aliases, the candidate formula, tetrahedral wording, dimension-jump language, and the K4 incidence formulation. The closest published exact result is the planar collapse formula, whose value is strictly smaller for 2<p<infinity. The current and immediate-prior own ledgers were checked; the only direct overlap is the isolated p=4 special case, which is subsumed but does not imply the continuum theorem.
residual_risks: Bibliographic and semantic-index searches cannot establish absolute novelty.
An equivalent theorem may exist under complete-graph p-energy or simplex terminology without the J_in notation.
The own p=4 special case is subsumed; the originality claim is specifically for the all-p theorem and its interpolation mechanism.

value.rationale: The result gives a closed exact law for an entire classical scale of Banach spaces rather than one exponent or one polygon. Its proof identifies the K4 incidence operator as the controlling structure, yielding a common tetrahedral extremizer for every super-Hilbert exponent. The strict comparison with the exact planar formula shows a genuine dimension-sensitive phenomenon throughout 2<p<infinity, which is mathematically informative beyond the numerical evaluation itself.
risks: The complementary higher-dimensional sub-Hilbert regime 1<p<2 remains unresolved here.
